svg.title: Fadecandy system overview: one Raspberry Pi, one Fadecandy, eight LED runs, one 5 V supply
svg.desc: The Raspberry Pi 3B+ connects to a Fadecandy board over USB. Each of the Fadecandy's eight channels leaves the board as a pair: a yellow DATA wire to the DI pad of one 64-pixel WS2812B run, and a black GND wire from that same channel's minus pin, twisted with it and landed on the GND bus alongside that run's own ground lead. There are eight such pairs, not eight lone data wires. The 5 V power supply feeds a red +5 V bus and a black GND bus that power the runs directly. Each run has four power legs, not two: a red and a black at its DI end and a red and a black at its far end, with both of that run's reds landing on the same single 6 A branch fuse. The feeder from the supply's V-plus terminal to the bus passes through a 40 A main fuse, and both bus bars are solid bars. Strip current flows only between the supply and the runs; it never passes through the Fadecandy or the Pi. For these eight runs the supply must be the sompom S-300-5, 60 A, which they load to 51 per cent; the 30 A LETOUR S-150-5 would be at 102 per cent of its rating and must not be used here.
svg.text: Diagram 1 - System overview: one control point, eight runs
Strip current flows only between the 5 V supply and the runs. It never passes through the Fadecandy or the Pi.
8 × DATA - one yellow wire per Fadecandy channel, ch 0 … ch 7
8 × GND - one black wire per channel, twisted with its DATA. Mandatory.
Android app talks to it over Wi-Fi / LAN
its own 5 V PSU - not the LED supply
sompom S-300-5 (5 V, 60 A) - 30.7 A is 51 %: use this
LETOUR S-150-5 (5 V, 30 A) - 102 %: DO NOT
Open-frame: MUST be enclosed and earthed.
Set output to 5.00 V with a meter - see § Safety.
V+ → +5 V bus V− → GND bus
Mains in on the far side, behind a barrier.
The Fadecandy carries no strip current.
Its J2 header has GND and DATA pins only - there is no
+5 V pin on it. Strip current leaves the supply's V+, goes
through the LEDs, and returns to the supply's V−.
Why the ground tie is mandatory
The DATA signal is a voltage measured against ground. The
Fadecandy drives it against ITS ground; each WS2812B reads
it against the SUPPLY's ground. If those two grounds are not
bonded, the LEDs have no reference, and the run will show
nothing, flicker, or display garbage colours.
Data and ground always travel together. Always.
Every run has FOUR power legs: +5 V and GND at its DI end, and +5 V and GND again at its far end. Both of a run’s reds land on that run’s ONE 6 A fuse.
Your strips have solder pads at the DI end only, so the far-end pair means opening and resealing about 18 sealed silicone sleeves. § 6.3 gives the one
alternative: feed the DI end alone under a 25 % brightness cap, which asks exactly as much of the strip as full white fed from both ends does.
